abstract: Bernstein-Vazirani algorithm (the one-query algorithm) can identify a completely specified linear Boolean function using a single query to the oracle with certainty. The first aim of the paper is to show that if the provided Boolean function is affine, then one more query to the oracle (the two-query algorithm) is required to identify the affinity of the function with certainty. The second aim of the paper is to show that if the provided Boolean function is incompletely defined, then the one-query and the two-query algorithms can be used as bounded-error quantum polynomial algorithms to identify certain classes of incompletely defined linear and affine Boolean functions respectively with probability of success at least $2/3$.
claim: For a completely specified n-input affine Boolean function f(x) = a.x XOR b, identify all coefficients a and the offset b with certainty using at most two oracle queries.
interface:
Write one Python module that defines:

  build_circuits(spec: dict) -> list[QuantumCircuit]
  postprocess(counts_list: list[dict[str, int]], spec: dict) -> {"a": list[int], "b": int}

spec = {"n": <number of input bits>, "shots": <shots per circuit>}.

The black box is available ONLY as an opaque gate: `from a2m_task import oracle`, then
`qc.append(oracle(n + 1), [0, 1, ..., n - 1, t])`. It acts as U_f|x>|y> = |x>|y XOR f(x)>,
x on the n listed input qubits (qubit i carries x_i), y on the last listed qubit, where
f(x) = a_0 x_0 XOR ... XOR a_{n-1} x_{n-1} XOR b. You cannot inspect a or b. Every appended
oracle gate counts as one query. Circuits must end in measurements of the bits you need.

The runner simulates each returned circuit `spec["shots"]` times against a hidden (a, b) and
passes their Qiskit counts dicts, in the same order, to postprocess. Qiskit bitstrings are
little-endian: the last character is classical bit 0. Return a[i] for input bit i and the
offset b. Gates must come from Qiskit's standard library (or circuits built from them).
notes: Scope: completely specified functions only; the incompletely defined case in the abstract is out of scope. Development case, not held out.
